target: Windows release readiness for Photo Curator

categories.name: Functional correctness
categories.description: Scan, duplicate detection, delete, undo, rename, and export behave correctly on Windows for the documented workflows.

categories.name: Data and file safety
categories.description: No realistic path to irrecoverable data loss; destructive actions are recoverable via the OS trash and Undo Delete, and the catalog stays consistent with disk state.

categories.name: Architecture and maintainability
categories.description: Service boundaries, dependency direction, and error handling remain coherent and are not being eroded by point fixes.

categories.name: Test quality and verification depth
categories.description: Automated tests exercise real behavior (not tautologies), and destructive workflows have host-verified evidence, not worker assertions alone.

categories.name: Performance and scalability
categories.description: Scan and duplicate detection scale acceptably for realistic library sizes without blocking the UI thread.

categories.name: UX and accessibility
categories.description: Dialogs, keyboard shortcuts, and status messaging are clear, and destructive actions are confirmed before they happen.

categories.name: Packaging, documentation, and release readiness
categories.description: Declared runtime dependencies, current docs, current test counts, and accurate unsupported-platform messaging for a Windows release.

hard_caps.description: Any realistic path where a user's files are permanently lost (bypassing OS trash / Undo Delete) caps the total score at 59 regardless of other category scores.
If the Windows project venv native test suite does not pass, the total score is capped at 69.
If Delete Duplicates and Undo Delete are not independently host-verified end-to-end through the real UI (not just worker assertion), the total score is capped at 84.

windows_platform_rule: Windows may score 100 only if destructive actions (delete/undo) on macOS and Linux are either disabled outright, or accurately documented and surfaced in the UI as unsupported on those platforms. A score of 100 is not permitted if non-Windows destructive behavior is undefined, silently different, or falsely described as recoverable when it is not.
review_protocol: You are a read-only reviewer scoring Photo Curator's Windows release readiness against rubric-v1 (photo-curator-windows-release-readiness). Score each of the 7 categories from 0 to its stated maximum, citing current file:line evidence for every deduction and every full-marks category. List every finding with a severity of P0, P1, P2, P3, or info, each with a concrete file and line number. Apply the rubric's hard caps if their conditions are met, and explain which cap (if any) applies. State plainly whether macOS/Linux destructive actions are disabled or accurately presented as unsupported, and flag it as a P0 finding if they are falsely presented as recoverable or silently diverge from Windows behavior. Do not assert that a destructive workflow (delete/undo) has been verified end-to-end unless you can point to host-generated verification evidence (a structured JSON result and screenshots produced by a real, host-executed UI run) that already exists; a worker-only claim of manual testing is not evidence and must not raise the test_quality_verification score or clear the unverified_core_destructive_workflow cap. Never modify the rubric, the validators, or the tests to make scoring easier. Report counts of test files/functions and documentation files you actually observe in the current repository state, not remembered or assumed counts. Output your findings as the machine-readable score JSON schema documented in ringer-100/README.md, with category scores, a total, findings with file/line/severity, host_gates left as your best current knowledge (the host verification step is authoritative and may override you), docs_test_count, runtime_dependencies_declared, unsupported_platform_messaging_accurate, and discretionary_override always false. You do not have authority to grant a discretionary override; if you believe one is warranted, say so in a finding instead.
